plantillas.chip.title: Show or hide: {nome}
plantillas.coverHelp: Design of the first page. Uses the same variables (school, course, head of department, role, date…) and the course logo via \logocentro. The LaTeX above must contain {{PORTADA}}; if empty, Lua uses its own cover. Applies to PDF and .tex only.
plantillas.descartar: This template has unsaved changes. Discard them?
plantillas.desfacer.ia.title: Go back to the state before the last AI change
plantillas.estiloHelp: The document design goes here, not in Lua's code: paragraph and title formatting, the schedule labels (\chip, \mesbadge, trimestre environment), the minutes header (\actacab, \actasecc, \actasinaturas...). Empty, Lua uses its own style; if you write something it replaces it entirely (start from Lua's with the button below). Task colours (tf-*, tt-*, tb-*, tc-*), gris-linea, gris-texto, \fontchip and \logocentro always come from Lua. It only applies to the PDF and the .tex.
plantillas.imagesHelp: They are stored with the template (not next to the course), so they work for any schedule wherever the file is. You can add several at once: images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF…, and RAW, SVG or HEIC if a converter is installed) and PDFs, which do not lose quality. In LaTeX use the name as is, e.g. \includegraphics{logotipo.pdf}; in Word/ODT, @imaxe logotipo.pdf 10.
plantillas.intro: The template decides the report layout: header with the logo and the school name, footer with the phone numbers and the name of the counsellor, margins… The course stays the same. It applies to the preview and to everything you export: PDF, LaTeX, Markdown, Word and OpenDocument. Export a template and import it on another computer so the whole department uses the same style.
plantillas.introHelp: Text of the “Introduction” section. You can use variables such as {{CENTRO}}, {{CURSO}} and {{DEPARTAMENTO}}; a blank line separates paragraphs. If the course has its own introduction, that one wins. Empty = Lua's text.
plantillas.latexHelp: Write {{CORPO}} wherever you want the report to go (index, introduction, schedule and development). If you do not add \documentclass, Lua adds its own preamble (enough for header and footer; it already loads fancyhdr); if you do, you are in charge and Lua only adds the packages and definitions the report needs. The first and last pages are designed below and go wherever you put {{PORTADA}} and {{SINATURA}}; without those markers Lua uses its own cover and signature. Put the school's fixed data as variables: {{TELEFONO}}, {{CORREO}}… Lua fills them in on its own, from the course and the school: {{CENTRO}}, {{LOCALIDADE}}, {{CURSO}}, {{DEPARTAMENTO}}, {{XEFE}} (or {{ORIENTADOR}}), {{CARGO}}, {{TITULO}}, {{DATA}}, {{DATA_LONGA}}, {{DATA_INICIO}}, {{DATA_FIN}}, {{ANO}} and {{FICHEIRO}}; if a variable with the same name has a value in the template, that value wins. The course logo is set with \logocentro[height=2cm].
plantillas.markdownHelp: Same {{CORPO}} and same variables, but in Markdown. If you leave it empty, the .md comes out without a layout. Images are referenced here as images/logo.png.
plantillas.name: Name
plantillas.needBody: {{CORPO}} is missing: without it Lua does not know where to put the report.
plantillas.noVars: No variables. Add one so a fixed value (the phone number, the school email…) can be changed without touching the LaTeX.
plantillas.noneDesc: The report comes out with Lua's default layout.
plantillas.ofi.axuda: Lua generates the document’s information; the look in Word and OpenDocument (font, colours, cover, header and footer) belongs to the template. Anything left empty uses Lua’s default design. You can use the same variables ({{CENTRO}}, {{CURSO}}…).
plantillas.ofi.cabeceira: Header (on every page except the cover)
plantillas.ofi.caixaAxuda: The header and footer can hold several logos in a row: one line per element, like “@imaxe logo1.png 10”, “@imaxe logo2.pdf 10” (height in mm; PNG, JPEG or PDF from this template’s image folder), text with variables, and “@esquerda”, “@centro” or “@dereita”.
plantillas.ofi.marxesAxuda: Leave line spacing and margins empty to use Lua's defaults (1.15 and 2.5 cm in Word; 2 cm in OpenDocument).
plantillas.ofi.pe: Footer text (next to the page number)
plantillas.ofi.portadaAxuda: One line per element: @logo 35 (course logo, height in mm), @imaxe nome.png 30 (an image of this template), @espazo 12, # Title, ## Subtitle, --- (rule), ### Highlighted line and plain text. Empty = the default cover.
plantillas.pdfVectorial: Vector: it does not lose quality in the report PDF. In Word/OpenDocument a pixel image of its page 1 is used.
plantillas.previewNoPages: It compiled, but the preview could not be drawn (pdftoppm is missing).
plantillas.save.title: Save the template and close the editor (Ctrl+Enter)
plantillas.savingFirst: Saving the template before adding the image…
plantillas.sen.datos: There is no data for this template. Close this window and open it again.
plantillas.signatureHelp: Design of the document's closing block (date, who signs and role). It goes at the end, without its own page; if you want one, start the fragment with \clearpage. The LaTeX above must contain {{SINATURA}}; if empty, Lua uses its own signature block. Applies to PDF and .tex only.
plantillas.textosHelp: Lua generates the content; the fixed texts of the document (section titles, "No tasks", the minutes labels...) are changed here, in PDF, Word, OpenDocument and Markdown. Empty = Lua's text (the grey one). The variables {{CENTRO}}, {{CURSO}}, {{DEPARTAMENTO}}... and those listed for each text can be used.

formularios.flx.intro.texto: Each field appears in the document according to its type: sections are headings, simple values go in a data sheet, and long texts and tables get their own heading. That is enough for most forms.
formularios.flx.intro.texto2: Customise the pipelines if you want to calculate something (averages, weighted marks, percentages), filter or sort a table, build sentences, show a block only in some cases or change the document order.
formularios.dis.asistente.label: Design assistant
formularios.asistente.label: Data assistant
asistente.tf.benvida: I design forms and pipelines. Attach with the clip a document you already have (a report, minutes, a mark sheet…) and I will work out the fields, tables and calculations from it; or describe what you need. Changes go into the designer draft and you decide whether to save them.
asistente.tf.nota: You can undo the last change with the “Undo AI change” button. If the document has calculations, check them carefully: always test what the assistant gives you.
asistente.tf.ph: Describe the form you want, or ask for changes: “add a students table”, “calculate the average mark”… If you press a card, this is added as an extra instruction.
asistente.tf.crear: Create a form from a description
formularios.nodo.constante.axuda: A text or number you type (e.g. a weight 0.4 or a pass mark 5).
formularios.nodo.calcular.axuda: Does a calculation with the incoming numbers (a, b, c...). Operators + - * / % ^ and comparisons; functions min, max, abs, sqrt, round(x,n), suma, media, se(cond,a,b). Decimal point: 0.4.
formularios.nodo.agregar.axuda: Gets a number from a table: sum, average, minimum, maximum or how many rows there are.
formularios.nodo.filtrar.axuda: Keeps only the table rows that meet a condition.
formularios.nodo.ordenar.axuda: Sorts the table rows by a column.
formularios.nodo.columnas.axuda: Keeps only some table columns (in the order you choose).
formularios.nodo.unir.axuda: Builds a sentence from the incoming values: in the template write {{a}}, {{b}}... where each goes.
formularios.nodo.comparar.axuda: Gives yes or no by comparing two values. Useful to hide a block (the “if” input of the blocks).
formularios.nodo.titulo.axuda: A heading in the document. Type fixed text or connect a text.
formularios.nodo.paragrafo.axuda: A Markdown text. It does not appear if empty.
formularios.nodo.ficha.axuda: “label: value” pairs one under another. Empty values are skipped.
formularios.nodo.taboa.axuda: Shows a table. It does not appear if it has no rows.
formularios.nodo.lista.axuda: A bulleted list with the values of a table column.
formularios.nodo.grafico.axuda: A chart. Pick the type (pie, donut, bars, lines...) and give it data: either a table (category column + value columns) or several loose quantities, each with its own label. It does not appear if there is no data.
formularios.cfg.grafico.columna.axuda: Only if you connect a table.
formularios.cfg.grafico.columnas.axuda: Each column is a series. Pie and donut use only the first.
formularios.nodo.imaxe.axuda: Shows an image. It does not appear if there is none.

asistente.tfd.benvida: I fill in the form with made-up data so you can try it out, or change what is already written. You can attach documents with a paperclip (a syllabus, a past exam…) for me to take into account, useful for designing exams and practice exercises. I can only see this form, its data and the documents you attach, and only while it is in design mode.
asistente.tfd.nota: You can undo what I do with the program’s history (Ctrl+Z). When the form goes to production, this assistant disappears.
